facts.claim: Saint Anthony of Padua was born in Lisbon in 1195 (as Fernando Martins de Bulhões), died on 13 June 1231 and his feast day is 13 June.
Britannica says Saint Anthony is the patron saint of Portugal and Padua and is famously invoked for the return of lost things; it does not call him a matchmaking saint or mention Brazil.
facts.conflicts: Brief asks for 'santo casamenteiro' (matchmaking saint) in Brazil; Britannica only links matchmaking to his feast-day festival in Lisbon. Brazilian matchmaking role stays 'often told' unless batch B or a Brazilian source confirms.

facts.claim: In Lisbon, the Saint Anthony festival around 13 June includes matchmaking traditions (giving a basil plant carrying a love message) and a televised wedding ceremony of dozens of couples.
Michaelis defines 'chá de panela' as a gathering, usually of women, at which a bride about to marry receives gifts for her new home from her friends; it lists 'chá de cozinha' as a synonym.

Michaelis lists 'chá de bebê' (also 'chá de berço') as a related gathering where guests bring gifts for an expected baby; no wedding-related variants such as chá de lingerie or chá bar appear in the entry.
Priberam defines 'madrinha' as a woman who serves as a witness at a baptism or wedding, and 'afilhado' as a person who has a padrinho or madrinha (of baptism, wedding, etc.).
Michaelis defines 'aliança' (among other senses) as a ring used as a symbol of engagement (noivado) or marriage (casamento). The entry does not say which hand it is worn on.
Michaelis defines 'noivado' as the relationship between two people who are going to marry, the time it lasts, and the occasion when the commitment is made official, generally with a party.

Priberam's related entry 'paraninfo' is defined as the groom's padrinho; 'talanqueira' records an old custom in the Miranda region (Portugal, not Brazil) where the padrinho paid so the wedding party could pass. Use only the 'paraninfo' definition, not the Portuguese regional custom.

insider_details.detail: Because 'noivado' covers both the engagement period and the party that makes it official, Brazilian families may expect an engagement celebration before the wedding; ask the couple early whether one is planned so guest travel is not doubled up.

An 'aliança' is the ring itself, used for both engagement and marriage, so the same band can carry through from noivado to wedding day; the hand-switch custom is often told rather than documented and should be written that way.

A chá de panela (also called chá de cozinha) is traditionally a gift gathering for the bride's new home, usually among women; for a destination wedding it is normally held at home before the couple travel, so it rarely affects the destination schedule.

Padrinhos and madrinhas are defined as wedding witnesses, so the honour is formal rather than decorative; confirm with the couple who will sign as legal witnesses versus who stands as an honorary padrinho, since legal witness numbers still need checking.

Saint Anthony's feast day is 13 June, the season of the June festivals; a June date may coincide with local festivities, which can be lovely for guests but worth checking against transport and accommodation demand.
